metadata.title: Simultaneous Analysis of Lasso and Dantzig Selector

nodes.name: Nonparametric regression model
nodes.statement: Sample $(Z_1,Y_1),\dots,(Z_n,Y_n)$ with $Y_i = f(Z_i) + W_i$, where $f:\mathcal{Z}\to\mathbb{R}$ is unknown, $Z_i$ are fixed in $\mathcal{Z}\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, and $W_i$ are Gaussian errors.
nodes.statement_clean: Fixed-design Gaussian regression with unknown regression function f.

nodes.name: Dictionary and design matrix
nodes.statement: A dictionary $\mathcal{F}_M = \{f_1,\dots,f_M\}$ with $M\ge 2$, design matrix $X = (f_j(Z_i))_{i,j}$, and ${\sf f}_\beta = \sum_{j=1}^M \beta_j f_j$ for $\beta\in\mathbb{R}^M$.
nodes.statement_clean: Finite dictionary of regressors and induced design matrix.

nodes.name: Empirical norm
nodes.statement: $\|g\|_n = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n g^2(Z_i)}$ for $g:\mathcal{Z}\to\mathbb{R}$, with $f_{\max} = \max_j \|f_j\|_n$, $f_{\min} = \min_j \|f_j\|_n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical L2 norm and extremal dictionary norms.

nodes.name: Sparsity index
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{M}(\beta) = \sum_{j=1}^M I_{\{\beta_j\ne 0\}} = |J(\beta)|$ where $J(\beta) = \{j: \beta_j\ne 0\}$. Smaller $\mathcal{M}(\beta)$ means sparser $\beta$.
nodes.statement_clean: Number of nonzero coordinates of beta.

nodes.name: Gram matrix
nodes.statement: $\Psi_n = \frac{1}{n}X^T X = \left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n f_j(Z_i)f_{j'}(Z_i)\right)_{j,j'}$, with $\phi_{\max}$ its maximal eigenvalue and $D = \mathrm{diag}\{\|f_1\|_n^2,\dots,\|f_M\|_n^2\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical Gram matrix, its maximal eigenvalue, and diagonal-norm matrix D.

nodes.name: Restricted eigenvalues
nodes.statement: $\phi_{\min}(u) = \min_{x: 1\le \mathcal{M}(x)\le u} \frac{x^T \Psi_n x}{|x|_2^2}$ and $\phi_{\max}(u) = \max_{x: 1\le \mathcal{M}(x)\le u} \frac{x^T \Psi_n x}{|x|_2^2}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Min/max eigenvalues of submatrices of size at most u.

nodes.name: Restricted correlations
nodes.statement: $\theta_{m_1,m_2} = \max\left\{\frac{c_1^T X_{I_1}^T X_{I_2} c_2}{n |c_1|_2 |c_2|_2}: I_1\cap I_2=\emptyset, |I_i|\le m_i, c_i\in\mathbb{R}^{I_i}\setminus\{0\}\right\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Maximal cross-correlation between disjoint subsets of regressors.

nodes.name: Weak sparsity property
nodes.statement: $f$ obeys weak sparsity if $\Lambda_s = \{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^M: \mathcal{M}(\beta)\le s, \|{\sf f}_\beta - f\|_n^2 \le \frac{C_0 f_{\max}^2 r^2}{\kappa^2}\mathcal{M}(\beta)\}$ is non-empty for some integer $s$ and $C_0<\infty$.
nodes.statement_clean: f admits a sparse beta whose bias term is bounded by the variance term.

nodes.name: Assumption RE(s, c_0)
nodes.statement: $\kappa(s,c_0) \triangleq \min_{|J_0|\le s} \min_{\bD\ne 0, |\bD_{J_0^c}|_1\le c_0|\bD_{J_0}|_1} \frac{|X\bD|_2}{\sqrt{n}|\bD_{J_0}|_2} > 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Restricted eigenvalue condition: positive definiteness on a restricted cone.

nodes.name: Assumption RE(s, m, c_0)
nodes.statement: $\kappa(s,m,c_0) \triangleq \min_{|J_0|\le s} \min_{\bD\ne 0, |\bD_{J_0^c}|_1\le c_0|\bD_{J_0}|_1} \frac{|X\bD|_2}{\sqrt{n}|\bD_{J_{01}}|_2} > 0$, where $J_{01}=J_0\cup J_1$ with $J_1$ indexing the $m$ largest-magnitude coordinates of $\bD$ outside $J_0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Stronger restricted eigenvalue with denominator over expanded index set J_{01}.

nodes.name: Assumption 1
nodes.statement: $\phi_{\min}(2s) > c_0\,\theta_{s,2s}$ for some integer $1\le s\le M/2$ and constant $c_0>0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sufficient condition for RE assumptions via min eigenvalue and restricted correlation.

nodes.name: Assumption 2
nodes.statement: $m\,\phi_{\min}(s+m) > c_0^2 s\,\phi_{\max}(m)$ for integers $1\le s\le M/2$, $m\ge s$, $s+m\le M$, and a constant $c_0>0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sufficient condition for RE assumptions using only min/max eigenvalues of small submatrices.

nodes.name: Assumption 3
nodes.statement: $\phi_{\min}(s) > 2 c_0\,\theta_{s,1}\sqrt{s}$ for $1\le s\le M$ and $c_0>0$.

nodes.name: Assumption 4
nodes.statement: $\phi_{\min}(s) > 2 c_0\,\theta_{1,1}\, s$ for $1\le s\le M$ and $c_0>0$.

nodes.name: Assumption 5
nodes.statement: All diagonal elements of $\Psi_n$ equal 1, and $\theta_{1,1} < \frac{1}{(1+2c_0)\,s}$ for some $1\le s\le M$ and $c_0>0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Mutual-coherence sufficient condition for RE(s,c_0), assuming unit diagonals.

nodes.name: Lasso optimization
nodes.statement: $\widehat\beta_L = \arg\min_{\beta\in\mathbb{R}^M}\left\{\widehat S(\beta) + 2r\sum_{j=1}^M \|f_j\|_n |\beta_j|\right\}$ where $\widehat S(\beta) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i (Y_i - {\sf f}_\beta(Z_i))^2$ and $r>0$.
nodes.statement_clean: L1-penalized least squares formulation of the Lasso.

nodes.name: Dantzig selector optimization
nodes.statement: $\widehat\beta_D = \arg\min\left\{|\beta|_1: \Big|\frac{1}{n}D^{-1/2}X^T(y-X\beta)\Big|_\infty \le r\right\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Min-L1-norm linear program subject to the Dantzig constraint.

nodes.name: Lasso estimator
nodes.statement: Convex optimization that returns the Lasso solution $\widehat\beta_L$ and the estimator $\widehat f_L(z) = \sum_{j=1}^M \widehat\beta_{j,L} f_j(z)$.

nodes.name: Dantzig selector
nodes.statement: Linear program returning the minimum-$\ell_1$ vector $\widehat\beta_D$ subject to the Dantzig constraint, yielding $\widehat f_D(z) = \sum_j \widehat\beta_{j,D} f_j(z)$.

nodes.name: KKT consequence for Lasso (Dantzig constraint)
nodes.statement: $\Big|\frac{1}{n}D^{-1/2}X^T(y - X\widehat\beta_L)\Big|_\infty \le r$.
nodes.statement_clean: Lasso solution automatically satisfies the Dantzig constraint.

nodes.name: Cone condition (c_0 inequality)
nodes.statement: $|\bD_{J_0^c}|_1 \le c_0 |\bD_{J_0}|_1$ holds with high probability for $\bD = \widehat\beta_L - \beta$ ($c_0=3$) or $\bD = \widehat\beta_D - \beta$ ($c_0=1$).
nodes.statement_clean: Residual lies in the c_0-cone supported on J_0.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.1 (Restricted positive definiteness)
nodes.statement: If Assumption 1 holds then RE(s,c_0) and RE(s,s,c_0) hold with $\kappa = \kappa_1(s,c_0) = \sqrt{\phi_{\min}(2s)}\left(1 - \frac{c_0\theta_{s,2s}}{\phi_{\min}(2s)}\right)$. If Assumption 2 holds then RE(s,c_0) and RE(s,m,c_0) hold with $\kappa = \kappa_2(s,m,c_0) = \sqrt{\phi_{\min}(s+m)}\left(1 - c_0\sqrt{\frac{s\phi_{\max}(m)}{m\phi_{\min}(s+m)}}\right)$. Moreover $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}|P_{01}X\bD|_2 \ge \kappa |\bD_{J_{01}}|_2$.

nodes.name: Lemma B.1 (Lasso oracle inequality on event A)
nodes.statement: With probability at least $1 - M^{1-A^2/8}$, for all $\beta\in\mathbb{R}^M$: $\|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2 + r\sum_j \|f_j\|_n |\widehat\beta_{j,L} - \beta_j| \le \|{\sf f}_\beta - f\|_n^2 + 4r\sum_{j\in J(\beta)}\|f_j\|_n |\widehat\beta_{j,L} - \beta_j|$, plus $|\frac{1}{n}X^T({\bmf} - X\widehat\beta_L)|_\infty \le 3rf_{\max}/2$ and $\mathcal{M}(\widehat\beta_L) \le 4\phi_{\max} f_{\min}^{-2}\|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2/r^2$.

nodes.name: Lemma B.2 (Dantzig cone and residual control)
nodes.statement: If $\beta$ satisfies the Dantzig constraint then $|\bD_{J_0^c}|_1 \le |\bD_{J_0}|_1$ for $\bD = \widehat\beta_D - \beta$. Furthermore, with probability at least $1 - M^{1-A^2/2}$ (under $A>\sqrt{2}$), $|\frac{1}{n}X^T({\bmf} - X\widehat\beta_D)|_\infty \le 2 r f_{\max}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (Approximate equivalence of Lasso and Dantzig)
nodes.statement: Under Gaussian noise, RE(s,1), $r = A\sigma\sqrt{\log M/n}$ with $A>2\sqrt{2}$, and $\mathcal{M}(\widehat\beta_L)\le s$: with probability $\ge 1 - M^{1-A^2/8}$, $\big|\|\widehat f_D - f\|_n^2 - \|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2\big| \le 16 A^2 \frac{\mathcal{M}(\widehat\beta_L)\sigma^2}{n}\frac{f_{\max}^2}{\kappa^2(s,1)}\log M$.
conclusions: Prediction losses of Lasso and Dantzig differ by at most an explicit oracle-rate quantity

nodes.name: Theorem 2 (Lasso prediction bounded by Dantzig prediction)
nodes.statement: Under the assumptions of Theorem 1 with RE(s,5) replacing RE(s,1), $\|f_j\|_n=1$, and $\mathcal{M}(\widehat\beta_D)\le s$: with probability $\ge 1 - M^{1-A^2/8}$, $\|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2 \le 10\|\widehat f_D - f\|_n^2 + 81 A^2 \frac{\mathcal{M}(\widehat\beta_D)\sigma^2}{n}\frac{\log M}{\kappa^2(s,5)}$.
conclusions: Lasso prediction loss bounded by 10 Dantzig prediction loss plus oracle term

nodes.name: Theorem 3 (Lasso sparsity oracle inequality, nonparametric)
nodes.statement: Under RE($s,(3+4/\eps)f_{\max}/f_{\min}$) and $r=A\sigma\sqrt{\log M/n}$ with $A>2\sqrt{2}$: with probability $\ge 1 - M^{1-A^2/8}$, $\|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2 \le (1+\eps)\inf_{\mathcal{M}(\beta)\le s}\left\{\|{\sf f}_\beta - f\|_n^2 + \frac{C(\eps)f_{\max}^2 A^2 \sigma^2}{\kappa^2}\,\frac{\mathcal{M}(\beta)\log M}{n}\right\}$.
conclusions: Sparsity oracle inequality for Lasso prediction in nonparametric regression

nodes.name: Proposition 1 (Dantzig sparsity oracle inequality, nonparametric)
nodes.statement: Under weak sparsity with $C_0<\infty$ and Assumption RE for $s\max\{C_1(\eps),1\}$: with probability $\ge 1 - M^{1-A^2/8}$, $\|\widehat f_D - f\|_n^2 \le (1+\eps)\inf_{\mathcal{M}(\beta)=s}\|{\sf f}_\beta - f\|_n^2 + C_2(\eps)\frac{f_{\max}^2 A^2 \sigma^2}{\kappa_0^2}\,\frac{s\log M}{n}$, with $C_1, C_2$ explicit constants.
conclusions: Sparsity oracle inequality for Dantzig prediction loss

nodes.name: Theorem 4 (Dantzig coefficient bounds, linear model)
nodes.statement: In the linear model with unit-diagonal Gram matrix and $\mathcal{M}(\bb^*)\le s$, under RE(s,1) and $A>\sqrt{2}$: with probability $\ge 1 - M^{1-A^2/2}$, $|\widehat\bb_D - \bb^*|_1 \le \frac{8A}{\kappa^2(s,1)}\sigma s\sqrt{\log M/n}$ and $|X(\widehat\bb_D - \bb^*)|_2^2 \le \frac{16 A^2}{\kappa^2(s,1)}\sigma^2 s\log M$. Under RE(s,m,1), for $1<p\le 2$, $|\widehat\bb_D - \bb^*|_p^p \le 2^{p-1}8\{1+\sqrt{s/m}\}^{2(p-1)} s\left(\frac{A\sigma}{\kappa^2(s,m,1)}\sqrt{\log M/n}\right)^p$.
assumptions: Linear model with unit Gram diagonal

nodes.name: Theorem 5 (Lasso coefficient bounds, linear model)
nodes.statement: In the linear model with unit Gram diagonal and $\mathcal{M}(\bb^*)\le s$, under RE(s,3) and $A>2\sqrt{2}$: with probability $\ge 1 - M^{1-A^2/8}$, $|\widehat\bb_L - \bb^*|_1 \le \frac{16A}{\kappa^2(s,3)}\sigma s\sqrt{\log M/n}$, $|X(\widehat\bb_L - \bb^*)|_2^2 \le \frac{16A^2}{\kappa^2(s,3)}\sigma^2 s\log M$, and $\mathcal{M}(\widehat\bb_L) \le \frac{64\phi_{\max}}{\kappa^2(s,3)} s$. Under RE(s,m,3), for $1<p\le 2$, $|\widehat\bb_L - \bb^*|_p^p \le 16\{1+3\sqrt{s/m}\}^{2(p-1)} s\left(\frac{A\sigma}{\kappa^2(s,m,3)}\sqrt{\log M/n}\right)^p$.
assumptions: Linear model with unit Gram diagonal

nodes.name: Theorem 6 (Sup-bound version of Theorem 4)
nodes.statement: Theorem 4 remains valid if $|\widehat\bb_D - \bb^*|_p^p$ is replaced by $\sup\{|\widehat\bb_D - \bb|_p^p: \bb\in\Lambda, \mathcal{M}(\bb)\le s\}$ and $|X(\widehat\bb_D - \bb^*)|_2^2$ by the analogous supremum, where $\Lambda$ is the set of vectors satisfying the Dantzig constraint.
conclusions: Bounds hold uniformly over all $s$-sparse vectors satisfying the Dantzig constraint

nodes.name: Corollary 1 (Soft Lasso oracle inequality)
nodes.statement: For all $n\ge 1$, $\eps>0$, $\gamma>0$: with probability $\ge 1 - M^{1-A^2/8}$, $\|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2 \le (1+\eps)\inf_{\beta\in\bar\Lambda_{s,\gamma,\eps}}\left\{\|{\sf f}_\beta - f\|_n^2 + \frac{C(\eps)f_{\max}^2 A^2\sigma^2}{\gamma^2}\frac{\mathcal{M}(\beta)\log M}{n}\right\}$, replacing the global RE constant with $\gamma$.

nodes.name: Corollary B.1 (Lasso cone inequality)
nodes.statement: Under the Lemma B.1 assumptions and $\|f_j\|_n=1$, in the linear regression model: with probability $\ge 1 - M^{1-A^2/8}$, $|\bD_{J_0^c}|_1 \le 3|\bD_{J_0}|_1$ where $\bD = \widehat\beta_L - \beta$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1 (Restricted positive definiteness)
nodes.statement: Partition $J_0^c$ into blocks of size $m$ ordered by descending magnitude; bound $|P_{01} X \bD_{J_k}|_2$ via $\sqrt{\phi_{\max}(m)}|\bD_{J_k}|_2$; sum the geometric tail using $|\bD_{J_{k+1}}|_2 \le |\bD_{J_k}|_1/\sqrt{m}$.

nodes.name: Block partition of $J_0^c$
nodes.statement: Partition $J_0^c = \cup_{k=1}^K J_k$ with $|J_k| = m$ for $k<K$, where $J_k$ collects the $m$ largest-magnitude coordinates of $\bD$ outside $\cup_{j<k} J_j$.

nodes.name: Block bound via $\phi_{\max}(m)$
nodes.statement: For $k\ge 1$, $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}|P_{01}X\bD_{J_k}|_2 \le \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}|X\bD_{J_k}|_2 \le \sqrt{\phi_{\max}(m)}\,|\bD_{J_k}|_2$ (used in part (ii); under Assumption 1 use $\theta_{s,2s}/\sqrt{\phi_{\min}(2s)}$ instead).

nodes.name: Geometric tail bound
nodes.statement: Using $|\bD_{J_{k+1}}|_2 \le |\bD_{J_k}|_1/\sqrt{m}$: $\sum_{k\ge 2} |\bD_{J_k}|_2 \le c_0\sqrt{s/m}\,|\bD_{J_{01}}|_2$, invoking the cone hypothesis $|\bD_{J_0^c}|_1 \le c_0 |\bD_{J_0}|_1$.

nodes.name: Combine and conclude
nodes.statement: Combining the estimates yields $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}|X\bD|_2 \ge \left(\sqrt{\phi_{\min}(s+m)} - c_0\sqrt{\phi_{\max}(m)}\sqrt{s/m}\right)|\bD_{J_{01}}|_2$ (part (ii)); part (i) follows analogously with $m\to s$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma B.1
nodes.statement: Define the high-probability event $\A = \bigcap_j \{2|V_j|\le r_{n,j}\}$ via Gaussian tails ($\PP(\A^c)\le M^{1-A^2/8}$). Manipulate the Lasso optimality inequality to get the oracle bound; combine with (\ref{dc}) for the residual sup-bound; use the KKT conditions plus eigenvalue argument for the sparsity bound.

nodes.name: Define the favorable event $\A$
nodes.statement: Set $V_j = n^{-1}\sum_i f_j(Z_i) W_i$ and $\A = \bigcap_j \{2|V_j|\le r_{n,j}\}$ with $r_{n,j} = r\|f_j\|_n$.

nodes.name: Gaussian tail bound on $\PP(\A^c)$
nodes.statement: $\PP(\A^c) \le M\,\PP(|\eta|\ge r\sqrt{n}/(2\sigma)) \le M\exp(-A^2\log M/8) = M^{1-A^2/8}$.

nodes.name: Manipulate Lasso optimality
nodes.statement: From $\widehat S(\widehat\beta_L) + 2\sum_j r_{n,j}|\widehat\beta_{j,L}| \le \widehat S(\beta) + 2\sum_j r_{n,j}|\beta_j|$, on $\A$ derive $\|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2 + \sum_j r_{n,j}|\widehat\beta_{j,L} - \beta_j| \le \|{\sf f}_\beta - f\|_n^2 + 2\sum_j r_{n,j}(|\widehat\beta_{j,L}-\beta_j| + |\beta_j| - |\widehat\beta_{j,L}|)$, then use $|a-b|+|b|-|a|=0$ for $j\notin J(\beta)$.

nodes.name: Derive sup-bound on residual
nodes.statement: On $\A$, $|\frac{1}{n}D^{-1/2}X^T W|_\infty \le r/2$; combined with the Lasso Dantzig constraint EP4.1, $|\frac{1}{n}X^T(\bmf - X\widehat\beta_L)|_\infty \le 3rf_{\max}/2$.

nodes.name: Sparsity bound via KKT
nodes.statement: Use Lasso KKT condition $|\frac{1}{n}\mathbf{x}_{(j)}^T(\bmf - X\widehat\beta_L)| \ge r\|f_j\|_n/2$ for $\widehat\beta_{j,L}\ne 0$ together with $\phi_{\max}$ to obtain $\mathcal{M}(\widehat\beta_L) \le 4\phi_{\max} f_{\min}^{-2}\|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2/r^2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma B.2
nodes.statement: Cone inequality is immediate from the definition of $\widehat\beta_D$ as the minimum-$\ell_1$ point in the Dantzig set. Sup-bound follows from event $\B = \{|\frac{1}{n}D^{-1/2}X^T W|_\infty \le r\}$ with $\PP(\B^c)\le M^{1-A^2/2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary B.1
nodes.statement: Apply the first inequality in (\ref{onA}) (Lemma B.1) and use $f = f_\beta$ in the linear regression model to obtain $|\bD_{J_0^c}|_1 \le 3|\bD_{J_0}|_1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Set $\bD = \widehat\beta_L - \widehat\beta_D$. Both sides of $\big|\|\widehat f_D - f\|_n^2 - \|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2\big|$ are bounded by combining a quadratic identity, Lemma B.2 sup-bound, the Dantzig cone (with $J_0 = J(\widehat\beta_L)$), and Assumption RE(s,1).

nodes.name: Quadratic identity for $\widehat\beta_L - \widehat\beta_D$
nodes.statement: Set $\bD = \widehat\beta_L - \widehat\beta_D$. Then $\frac{1}{n}|\bmf - X\widehat\beta_L|_2^2 = \frac{1}{n}|\bmf - X\widehat\beta_D|_2^2 - \frac{2}{n}\bD^T X^T(\bmf - X\widehat\beta_D) + \frac{1}{n}|X\bD|_2^2$.

nodes.name: Bound on cross term via Lemma B.2
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma B.2 inequality $|\frac{1}{n}X^T(\bmf - X\widehat\beta_D)|_\infty \le 2rf_{\max}$ to obtain $\|\widehat f_D - f\|_n^2 \le \|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2 + 4f_{\max}r|\bD|_1 - \frac{1}{n}|X\bD|_2^2$ with probability $\ge 1 - M^{1-A^2/2}$.

nodes.name: Cone inequality on $\bD$
nodes.statement: Since $\widehat\beta_L$ satisfies the Dantzig constraint, Lemma B.2 with $\beta = \widehat\beta_L$ gives $|\bD_{J_0^c}|_1 \le |\bD_{J_0}|_1$ where $J_0 = J(\widehat\beta_L)$.

nodes.name: Apply RE(s,1) to bound $|\bD|_1$ via $|X\bD|_2$
nodes.statement: By RE(s,1), $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}|X\bD|_2 \ge \kappa |\bD_{J_0}|_2$, hence $|\bD|_1 \le 2\sqrt{\mathcal{M}(\widehat\beta_L)}|\bD_{J_0}|_2 \le \frac{2\sqrt{\mathcal{M}(\widehat\beta_L)}}{\kappa\sqrt{n}}|X\bD|_2$.

nodes.name: Optimize quadratic in $|X\bD|_2$ -- one direction
nodes.statement: Substitute into PSP4.12 to get $\|\widehat f_D - f\|_n^2 \le \|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2 + 16 f_{\max}^2 r^2 \mathcal{M}(\widehat\beta_L)/\kappa^2$ by maximizing the linear-quadratic expression in $|X\bD|_2$.

nodes.name: Reverse direction via Lemma B.1
nodes.statement: Symmetric argument with roles of $\widehat\beta_L,\widehat\beta_D$ swapped, using Lemma B.1 sup-bound (\ref{dcf}) instead of (\ref{ll23}), yields $\|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2 \le \|\widehat f_D - f\|_n^2 + 9 f_{\max}^2 r^2 \mathcal{M}(\widehat\beta_L)/\kappa^2$, with probability $\ge 1 - M^{1-A^2/8}$.

nodes.name: Combine both directions
nodes.statement: Combining the two-sided bounds yields the announced symmetric inequality with constant $16 A^2$ (since $r^2 = A^2 \sigma^2 \log M/n$).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Set $\bD = \widehat\beta_L - \widehat\beta_D$, apply Lemma B.1 with $\beta = \widehat\beta_D$, then split into two cases depending on whether $\|\widehat f_D - f\|_n^2 > 2r|\bD_{J_0}|_1$ or not.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma B.1 with $\beta=\widehat\beta_D$
nodes.statement: $|\bD|_1 \le 4|\bD_{J_0}|_1 + \|\widehat f_D - f\|_n^2/r$ with probability $\ge 1 - M^{1-A^2/8}$, where $J_0 = J(\widehat\beta_D)$.

nodes.name: Case split on bias term
nodes.statement: Case (i): $\|\widehat f_D - f\|_n^2 > 2r|\bD_{J_0}|_1$. Case (ii): $\|\widehat f_D - f\|_n^2 \le 2r|\bD_{J_0}|_1$.

nodes.name: Case (i) closure
nodes.statement: Direct from inequality (\ref{e5}) with $f_{\max}=1$: $\|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2 \le 10\|\widehat f_D - f\|_n^2$, theorem holds.

nodes.name: Case (ii) cone setup
nodes.statement: From PSP4.18 we get $|\bD|_1 \le 6|\bD_{J_0}|_1$, hence $|\bD_{J_0^c}|_1 \le 5|\bD_{J_0}|_1$, allowing the use of RE(s,5).

nodes.name: Apply RE(s,5) and finish case (ii)
nodes.statement: RE(s,5) yields $|\bD|_1 \le \frac{6\sqrt{\mathcal{M}(\widehat\beta_D)}}{\kappa\sqrt{n}}|X\bD|_2$; substituting into (\ref{e5}) gives $\|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2 \le \|\widehat f_D - f\|_n^2 + 81 r^2 \mathcal{M}(\widehat\beta_D)/\kappa^2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3
nodes.statement: Fix $\beta$ with $\mathcal{M}(\beta)\le s$, set $\bD = D^{1/2}(\widehat\beta_L - \beta)$, $J_0 = J(\beta)$. From Lemma B.1, on event $\A$ derive a cone inequality, apply Assumption RE($s,(3+4/\eps)f_{\max}/f_{\min}$), and finish via decoupling argument $2xy\le x^2/b + by^2$.

nodes.name: Setup variables and apply Lemma B.1
nodes.statement: Set $\bD = D^{1/2}(\widehat\beta_L - \beta)$, $J_0 = J(\beta)$. From the first inequality of (\ref{onA}): $\|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2 + r|\bD|_1 \le \|{\sf f}_\beta - f\|_n^2 + 4r|\bD_{J_0}|_1$.

nodes.name: Case split on bias vs cone
nodes.statement: Case (a): $4r|\bD_{J_0}|_1 \le \eps\|{\sf f}_\beta - f\|_n^2$. Case (b): $\eps\|{\sf f}_\beta - f\|_n^2 < 4r|\bD_{J_0}|_1$.

nodes.name: Case (a) trivial closure
nodes.statement: In case (a), the result follows trivially from PSP4.23 since the cone term is dominated by the bias term.

nodes.name: Apply RE assumption
nodes.statement: Apply RE($s,(3+4/\eps)f_{\max}/f_{\min}$): $\kappa^2|\bD'_{J_0}|_2^2 \le \frac{1}{n}|X\bD'|_2^2 = \|\widehat f_L - {\sf f}_\beta\|_n^2$, where $\kappa = \kappa(s,(3+4/\eps)f_{\max}/f_{\min})$.

nodes.name: Decoupling inequality
nodes.statement: Apply $2xy \le x^2/b + by^2$ with $b>1$, $x = r\kappa^{-1}\sqrt{\mathcal{M}(\beta)}$, and $y\in\{\|\widehat f_L - f\|_n, \|{\sf f}_\beta - f\|_n\}$ to obtain $\|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2 \le \frac{b+1}{b-1}\|{\sf f}_\beta - f\|_n^2 + \frac{8b^2 f_{\max}^2}{(b-1)\kappa^2}r^2\mathcal{M}(\beta)$.

nodes.name: Choose $b = 1 + 2/\eps$
nodes.statement: Setting $b = 1 + 2/\eps$ yields the claimed sparsity oracle inequality with $C(\eps)$ derived from $b^2/(b-1)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1
nodes.statement: Use weak sparsity to find $\bar\beta$, apply Theorem 3 and (\ref{Lassom}) to bound $\mathcal{M}(\widehat\beta_L)$, then invoke Theorem 1 and Theorem 3 again.

nodes.name: Invoke weak sparsity
nodes.statement: Weak sparsity gives $\bar\beta\in\mathbb{R}^M$ with $\mathcal{M}(\bar\beta)\le s$ and $\|{\sf f}_{\bar\beta} - f\|_n^2 \le C_0 f_{\max}^2 r^2 \kappa^{-2}\mathcal{M}(\bar\beta)$.

nodes.name: Bound Lasso sparsity via Theorem 3 and Lemma B.1
nodes.statement: Combining Theorem 3 (TP4.3) with the sparsity bound (\ref{Lassom}) of Lemma B.1: $\mathcal{M}(\widehat\beta_L) \le C_1(\eps)\mathcal{M}(\bar\beta) \le C_1(\eps) s$, with probability $\ge 1 - M^{1-A^2/8}$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 1 to compare losses
nodes.statement: Theorem 1 (TP4.1) yields $\|\widehat f_D - f\|_n^2 \le \|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2 + \frac{16 C_1(\eps)f_{\max}^2 A^2 \sigma^2}{\kappa_0^2}\frac{s\log M}{n}$ where $\kappa_0 = \kappa(\max(C_1(\eps),1)s, 3+4/\eps)$.

nodes.name: Re-apply Theorem 3 to finish
nodes.statement: Applying TP4.3 once again to $\|\widehat f_L - f\|_n^2$ produces the stated oracle inequality with constant $C_2(\eps) = 16 C_1(\eps) + C(\eps)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4
nodes.statement: On event $\B$, use Lemma B.2 to deduce $\frac{1}{n}|X^T X \bD|_\infty \le 2r$ and the cone inequality with $c_0=1$. Bound $\frac{1}{n}|X\bD|_2^2$ by $4r\sqrt{s}|\bD_{J_0}|_2$ and apply RE(s,1). Derive $\ell_p$ bound using a tail-sum trick and RE(s,m,1).

nodes.name: Setup and event $\B$
nodes.statement: Set $\bD = \widehat\bb_D - \bb^*$, $J_0 = J(\bb^*)$. Lemma B.2 with $\beta = \bb^*$ gives, on $\B$ (probability $\ge 1 - M^{1-A^2/2}$): (i) $\frac{1}{n}|X^T X \bD|_\infty \le 2r$ and (ii) cone inequality with $c_0=1$.

nodes.name: Quadratic-form bound
nodes.statement: $\frac{1}{n}|X\bD|_2^2 = \frac{1}{n}\bD^T X^T X \bD \le \frac{1}{n}|X^T X \bD|_\infty |\bD|_1 \le 4r\sqrt{s}|\bD_{J_0}|_2$ via cone inequality and $|\bD_{J_0}|_1 \le \sqrt{s}|\bD_{J_0}|_2$.

nodes.name: Apply RE(s,1)
nodes.statement: RE(s,1) gives $\frac{1}{n}|X\bD|_2^2 \ge \kappa^2 |\bD_{J_0}|_2^2$, hence $\frac{1}{n}|X\bD|_2^2 \le 16 r^2 s/\kappa^2$ and $|\bD_{J_0}|_2 \le 4r\sqrt{s}/\kappa^2$, proving (\ref{th43}) and (\ref{th44}).

nodes.name: Apply RE(s,m,1) and conclude $\ell_p$ bound
nodes.statement: From RE(s,m,1) and PSP4.35: $|\bD_{J_{01}}|_2 \le 4r\sqrt{s}/\kappa^2$. Combine with the tail estimate to get $|\bD|_2^2 \le 16(1+c_0\sqrt{s/m})^2 (r\sqrt{s}/\kappa^2)^2$. Use $\sum a_j^p \le b_1^{2-p}b_2^{p-1}$ for $1<p\le 2$ to obtain (\ref{th42}).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5
nodes.statement: On event $\A$, apply Lemma B.1 with $\beta = \bb^*$, $\|{\sf f}_\beta - f\|_n = 0$ to get $\frac{1}{n}|X\bD|_2^2 \le 4r\sqrt{s}|\bD_{J_0}|_2$ and cone with $c_0=3$. Apply RE(s,3) and follow Theorem 4's argument with $c_0=3$.

nodes.name: Setup and apply Lemma B.1 with $\beta=\bb^*$
nodes.statement: Set $\bD = \widehat\bb_L - \bb^*$, $J_0 = J(\bb^*)$. Lemma B.1 with $\beta = \bb^*$ and $\|{\sf f}_\beta - f\|_n = 0$ yields $\frac{1}{n}|X\bD|_2^2 \le 4r\sqrt{s}|\bD_{J_0}|_2$ on event $\A$, and (\ref{l21}) with $c_0=3$.

nodes.name: Apply RE(s,3)
nodes.statement: By RE(s,3): $\frac{1}{n}|X\bD|_2^2 \le 16 r^2 s/\kappa^2$ and $|\bD_{J_0}|_2 \le 4r\sqrt{s}/\kappa^2$, with $\kappa = \kappa(s,3)$. The first matches (\ref{th54}).

nodes.name: Sparsity bound (\ref{th55})
nodes.statement: Combine (\ref{Lassom}) from Lemma B.1 with (\ref{th54}) to obtain $\mathcal{M}(\widehat\bb_L) \le \frac{64\phi_{\max}}{\kappa^2(s,3)} s$.

nodes.name: Derive $\ell_1$ and $\ell_p$ bounds
nodes.statement: Using (\ref{dl6a}) with $c_0=3$ gives (\ref{th53}). The $\ell_p$ bound (\ref{th52}) follows verbatim the Theorem 4 argument (PSP4.37, PSP4.38) with $c_0=3$ in (\ref{chain0}), (\ref{chain2}).
